newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada unveils new clean air measures.
newsitem.headline: Canada unveils new clean air measures.

text.p: Canadian Environment Minister Sergio Marchi outlined new measures on Monday to reduce pollutants from cars and trucks.
One of the regulations, to take effect at the start of 1999, will cut the content of the carcinogenic substance benzene in gasoline by half to a maximum of one percent.
Marchi, addressing a pollution workshop in Toronto, said it would reduce annual emissions by 3,000 metric tonnes or three million litres.

New regulations cutting sulphur in diesel will take effect at the start of 1998, he said. Sulphur in diesel for on-road vehicles, such as trucks and buses, will now be limited to 0.05 percent by weight.

Marchi's spokesman, Roger White, said this amounted to about a 50 percent reduction. Some diesel will be limited as at present to 0.02 percent sulphur, which creates urban smog and contributes to respiratory diseases.

He said that new motor vehicle emissions standards taking effect with the 1998 model year would cut the output of nitrogen oxides by 60 percent and exhaust hydrocarbons by 30 percent. These were announced last summer.
The minister also encouraged provinces to implement vehicle inspection programmes to reduce pollution.
Twenty percent of vehicles produce 80 percent of automotive pollution, and an out-of-tune car can be 2.5 times more polluting than a tuned-up one, he said.
